title: Microsoft Purview: run a Power Automate flow when a retention label's retention period ends (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The summary incorrectly limits changes to administrators who select a flow. Configured flows can also affect document users, including notifying document authors or moving their documents; the rollout details, configuration route and licensing prerequisites are supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions, renamed or moved file
claims.claim: Without the resilience action, a renamed or moved file can make the flow fail because the file cannot be found.
claims.quote: This additional action is required for files that you move or rename after an instance of the flow is triggered but your specified compliance actions aren't completed.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'Learn says that if a file is moved or renamed after the flow is triggered but before its compliance actions complete, the flow fails to find it unless it uses the "Trigger a new instance of the flow if an item can’t be located" action.' This preserves the source's timing qualification without changing the existing recommendation to add the action.

claims.claim: The recommended resilience action goes before relabel or delete compliance actions.
claims.quote: Although optional, we recommend you always add the Trigger a new instance of the flow if an item can't be located action before Relabel an item at the end of retention and Deletes an item at the end of retention.

claims.claim: Apply a retention label on the item is independent of the end-of-retention scenario and equivalent to manually applying a label.
claims.quote: This action is independent from this scenario that applies actions at the end of the retention period. Instead, it's the equivalent to manually applying a retention label.

claims.claim: The Apply a retention label on the item action applies the label immediately.
claims.quote: The label is applied immediately.
